description: Enforces strict adherence to statutory or court-mandated time schedules for admissions, counseling, and institutional approvals in professional education, prohibiting belated actions even if seats remain vacant.
application_scenario: Use when a party seeks a judicial directive to permit mid-stream admissions, conduct extra rounds of counseling to fill vacant seats, or process an incomplete institutional application after the prescribed regulatory cut-off date has passed.
reasoning_flow: Identify the statutory or court-mandated time schedule and specific cut-off dates governing the admission process, counseling round, or institutional approval.
Determine whether the requested relief (e.g., belated admission, extra counseling round, or curing a defective application) falls past the strict deadline.

Evaluate and dismiss equitable arguments such as the existence of unfilled seats, institutional financial loss, or sympathetic hardship, prioritizing uniform academic standards and the integrity of the curriculum timeline.
Deny the relief and enforce the cut-off date strictly, ruling that vacant seats cannot be filled after the deadline and mid-stream admissions are legally impermissible.
example_application: A medical college petitions the court to hold an additional mop-up counseling round to fill 50 vacant postgraduate seats a week after the Supreme Court-mandated national deadline. The court dismisses the petition, ruling that the sanctity of the academic time schedule supersedes the financial or equitable loss of unfilled seats, and bars any admissions beyond the cut-off date.
shared_pattern: In each case, the court identifies a hard deadline for an academic or regulatory milestone, observes that the petitioner seeks to bypass this deadline (often citing vacant seats or curable defects), and ultimately rejects the plea to preserve the integrity of the schedule and prevent unauthorized mid-stream or belated entries.
scope_exclusions: Do not use for ordinary civil limitation condonations under general limitation acts (covered by LF024) or where the expert regulatory body itself has legally and prospectively extended the deadline prior to its expiration.
